evidence: /root/.claude/settings.json:380 binds PreToolUse Edit/Write matcher to: python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py" → resolves to /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py (md5 3544ce61a24d03eeba23da4ab8636e10, 13330 bytes, mtime Apr 25 — predates W1-patch).

/root/travel-planner/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py is a DIFFERENT file (md5 4c6ba4d52112cb8b019298cd08fad5a6, 9082 bytes, mtime May 13 22:23 — modified by W1-patch). It contains _bypass_reason at line 46 honoring both BYPASS_QUALITY_GATE=1 env-var and .claude/dev-registry/dev-*/bypass-quality-gate.flag sentinels.
grep 'BYPASS_QUALITY_GATE|sentinel|bypass-quality-gate|_bypass' /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py → 0 hits. The binding global hook has zero bypass code.

Single Edit attempt during this dispatch (Bug 2 Tier-0 gaode_id fast-path, +8 lines inside _get_timeline_time): blocked with 'Worsened: Function _get_timeline_time grew from 40 to 48 lines'. No bypass audit line emitted to stderr, confirming the binding hook never executed any bypass code path.
blocking_issues.why_blocking: All three Bug-1/2/3 target edits add lines to functions already over the 30-line cap (_merge_day_data 581 lines; _get_timeline_time 40 lines; _read_react_template 1822 lines for Bug-3 JSX changes). The binding global hook's no-net-worsening grandfather mode allows only edits that strictly do not grow any per-function metric — which forbids every prescribed surgical fix in W2's write-set.
required_resolution_options: (A, RECOMMENDED — minimum-diff) Orchestrator (or user) ports the 18-line _bypass_reason+_bypass_quality_gate block from the project-local hook into /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py and wires the check into main() before collect_violations(). Verifiable via the stdin-payload test above. After this lands, re-dispatch W2 with no other changes — the existing sentinel at .claude/dev-registry/dev-20260513-090000/bypass-quality-gate.flag will trip the bypass. Caveat per Subagent Hook Discipline: the W2 subagent MUST NOT edit hook files itself; this resolution is for the orchestrator or user.

(B) Orchestrator updates /root/.claude/settings.json:380 to invoke the project-local hook (/root/travel-planner/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py) instead of the global one. Same hook-edit prohibition applies — orchestrator/user only.

(C) Run W7 FIRST (mechanical refactor of _merge_day_data into 9 small helpers in scripts/lib/render_day_data.py). After the renderer shrinks under 800 lines and individual functions go under 30 lines, re-dispatch W2 to land Bug 1/2/3 inside the new helper modules. Inverts the BA-spec-prescribed W2→W7 sequencing and complicates AC12's 'byte-identical merged-dict pre/post refactor' invariant (no post-W2 baseline to diff against). Not recommended.

(D) Out-of-scope alternative — would require W2 to author NEW small modules plus a shrinking refactor on generate-html-interactive.py that nets zero or negative per-function-line delta. Resembles W7 scope creep and is forbidden by 'File-disjoint vs all OTHER workers' constraint.
blocking_issues.recommended_resolution: (A). Single-file port preserves W1-patch's intent, matches AC-DISPATCH alternative_mechanism, and unblocks W2 with no other changes. Estimated 18 lines of edit to one hook file.

recommendations: Orchestrator: execute resolution (A) — port _bypass_reason()+_bypass_quality_gate() from /root/travel-planner/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py into /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py and wire it at the top of main() before collect_violations(). Verify with: echo '<edit-payload>' | python3 /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py → must exit 0 with 'QUALITY GATE BYPASSED via sentinel' audit line.

After (A) lands, re-dispatch W2 with the identical retry-dispatch prompt. The existing sentinel at /root/travel-planner/.claude/dev-registry/dev-20260513-090000/bypass-quality-gate.flag will be honored. Two sentinel mirrors now exist on the host (project-local + /root/.claude/dev-registry/dev-20260513-090000/bypass-quality-gate.flag created during this dispatch as a diagnostic remediation attempt); either will trip the bypass once the binding hook has the code.

Audit gap: W1-patch's dev report should have included a positive end-to-end test (e.g., 'echo <payload> | python3 <BINDING_HOOK_AS_PER_SETTINGS> exits 0') instead of merely verifying the file it edited honors the sentinel. The actual hook file that fires is determined by settings.json, not by which file W1-patch chose to edit. Future hook patches should resolve the binding via settings.json and patch THAT file.

Defensive analysis: this is exactly the failure mode that round-2 OBJ-4 warned about ('W1→W2 env-var coupling fragility'). The chosen sentinel-file alternative was supposed to make the coupling robust; it failed because the hook-file selection itself was the brittle link. A more robust design would have the orchestrator dispatch both (i) inject env-var into subagent execve, AND (ii) create sentinel, AND have W1 patch BOTH plausible hook locations OR (better) resolve binding-hook path from settings.json before editing.
